claims.claim: Intl.DateTimeFormat('he-IL') resolves to the Gregorian calendar; the Hebrew calendar is requested via the `ca` Unicode extension key, e.g. Intl.DateTimeFormat('he-IL-u-ca-hebrew'), which formats 2026-09-20 as '9 בתשרי 5787'.
claims.raw_snippet: The calendar to use, such as "chinese", "gregory", "persian", and so on. For a list of supported calendar types, see Intl.supportedValuesOf(); the default is locale dependent. This option can also be set through the ca Unicode extension key; if both are provided, this options property takes precedence.

claims.claim: Under the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (rule W4) a single European separator such as a hyphen between two numbers becomes part of the number, so 050-321-4450 stays one LTR run in RTL text, while space-separated groups (050 321 4450) and a +972 prefix are reordered.
claims.raw_snippet: A single European separator between two European numbers changes to a European number.
claims.verification_note: Rendered in Chromium (Playwright, 2026-09-25) inside <html dir=rtl>: '050-321-4450' displays in order; '050 321 4450' displays as 4450 321 050; '+972 50-321-4450' displays as 50-321-4450 972+ (left-to-right glyph order measured with Range.getBoundingClientRect).

claims.claim: unicode-bidi: bidi-override lays characters out strictly in the direction value and ignores the implicit bidi algorithm, so Latin text inside an RTL override renders reversed; it is for forcing a known order, not for mixed content.

claims.raw_snippet: The directionality is calculated using the P2 and P3 rules of the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm.

claims.claim: The he-IL currency format carries right-to-left marks (U+200F) around the number and the currency sign, so it is laid out for an RTL context; forcing dir=ltr on it moves the shekel sign to the other side of the number.
claims.verification_note: Node 20: Intl.NumberFormat('he-IL',{style:'currency',currency:'ILS'}).format(1234) === '\u200f1,234.00\u00a0\u200f\u20aa'. Chromium render in <html dir=rtl>: bare and <bdi> both place the shekel sign left of the digits; <span dir=ltr> places it right of them.
